calls.title: Nhat & Johnny
calls.summary: The team discussed key improvements in product visualization, notably in chart clarity and user interface for better data presentation. Significant enhancements were made to the line chart's opacity and tooltips, allowing for clearer comparison of current and previous values. Custom date range selection faced UX challenges, with discussions on color differentiation to reduce user confusion. There was a focus on bar chart visuals, analyzing overlay and offset techniques for clearer comparisons. Additionally, the big number display was expanded to allow multiple metrics, pending leadership input. Bugs in date input and legend customization were highlighted as needing resolution to maintain a smooth user experience. The meeting emphasized the prioritization of custom date range UX and bar chart improvements, along with plans for bug fixes and UI polishing.
calls.keywords: custom date range, bar chart, tooltip, big number metrics, UX design, time comparison
calls.action_items:
**Johnny Martinez**
Create and send Figma mockups for custom date range UI improvements to enhance user experience and address current UX challenges (10:20)
Capture and share screenshots of the discussed charts and tables to serve as design references for ongoing iterations (13:55)

**Nhat Ho**
Fix tooltip label display issues in custom date ranges where the selected range is not consistently highlighted, improving clarity (11:02)
Investigate and resolve bugs related to date range selection state resetting unexpectedly to ensure stable user interactions (12:09)
Consult with Jeremy to confirm design constraints and intended behavior for big number metrics display, particularly regarding allowance of multiple metrics or enforcing single metric with warnings (09:14)
Refine bar chart legend and tooltip behavior based on team feedback to improve clarity and user interaction (12:41)

calls.title: Nhat / Johnny
calls.summary: The team discussed adopting a user-friendly filter design inspired by Google Analytics to improve product analytics usability. Key decisions included using familiar date picker patterns to avoid user confusion and incorporating expandable pills for managing filters efficiently. They emphasized the importance of clear navigation, particularly in managing multiple product lines. Additionally, the incorporation of a dropdown search was proposed to streamline filter selection. Performance issues related to resource management were acknowledged, and collaborative efforts were planned, including sharing screenshots for design feedback. The overall goal is to simplify navigation, enhance user experience, and ensure smoother integration between independent products.
calls.keywords: Dashboard filters, Metric Explorer, UI design, experiment filters, date picker, filter pills
